geometry_edits.rationale: Recast the dominant mass as a continuous occupiable section rather than two visibly colliding bars.
Use a controlled stepped section to preserve height hierarchy while making the silhouette read as one continuous mass.
Orient the section so the long bar remains the primary occupiable datum.
Enlarge the court to create a readable public void and active ground threshold.
Align the opening with the verified access edge to strengthen frontage response.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the current bent bar logic with a form-making operation that can create one continuous dominant mass and avoid reading as two detached bars.
Reduce the bend so the main body reads as a single coherent gesture instead of a hard bifurcation.
Simplify the sectional articulation to strengthen form continuity.
Increase the carved void so the public threshold becomes legible and materially useful.
Keep the void aligned to the verified access side so the street edge becomes an active entry seam rather than a sealed front.

rationale: The candidate is not coherent enough as a neighborhood-living massing. Across the four views it reads as two separate rectilinear pieces rather than one dominant occupiable volume with a secondary support/void relation. The top and opposite views suggest the pieces are displaced and not convincingly unified, so the silhouette and spatial rule are weak. The blue frontage edge is acknowledged only indirectly; there is no strong public seam, court, or undercut that activates the access edge. Because the program requires an active ground threshold and usable public void, this proposal remains too generic and too sealed to pass as neighborhood living, even though the overall repair is geometrically clean and not visibly broken.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is a tall mixed-use prism; the candidate is much smaller and split into two separated bars, so only the sectional hierarchy is transferable.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stepped/tapered upper mass over a legible lower datum; use the section to organize a clear hierarchy without turning the whole object into a tower.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This is a tower precedent; the candidate is neighborhood living and should not drift toward a purely tower-like reading.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A single coherent vertical object can carry a controlled stepped or torqued profile while staying legible across views.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference is a low commercial pavilion; the candidate lacks the open threshold and reads more as two isolated masses.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A clear active ground edge and small projecting/void response at the street can support neighborhood-scale program.

warnings: Visible massing is split and semantically under-connected across views.
No legible public void or street threshold along the verified access edge.
The form trends toward generic bars/boxes rather than a clear neighborhood-living section.
Avoid reading the stepped/tapered language as automatically program-appropriate; the dominant issue is hierarchy and ground response.
